items.title: Is India's Mass IT Hiring Era Finally Over? | Point Break
items.summary:
Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu recently raised alarm over India's youth employment landscape, noting that capital previously allocated for headcount is now diverted toward AI infrastructure, servers, and compute. While Indian IT hiring showed a modest 6% year-on-year uptick and AI roles surged 33%, freshers now represent only 15% of total IT hiring compared to nearly 28% a few years ago. Mass campus recruitment drives and bench models are giving way to selective, capability-led hiring directly tied to client demand.

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Gaurav Vasu, Founder & CEO of UnearthInsight, and Sunil Padmanabh, Enterprise AI & GCC Strategist, to break down whether Indian IT is genuinely recovering or undergoing a permanent structural shift. They analyze the decline from peak campus hiring levels, the changing unit economics of IT services, the evolution of GCCs from cost centers to R&D hubs, and what the future holds for engineering graduates across tier-2 and tier-3 colleges.

Is AI productivity permanently altering the traditional IT employment model?

items.title: AI to Self-morph into a different AI configuration? How?
items.summary:
Can an AI override its objectives and primary goals? Self-morph into a different AI configuration? Leave its security guardrails behind? 
New video on agentic runtime morphisms. 
On the simple example of an AI Harness doing research experiments in a "secure" lab (smile).

The AI Harness: Memory, Control & Scientific Reasoning.

A capable, fixed language model (XLM) still cannot run a long, revisable research campaign by itself. Not because it lacks intelligence, but because three separate things are missing that no amount of in-context competence supplies:
 1.  A stateless call has no memory to found continuity on. 
 2.  Self-assessment cannot be made independent of itself no matter how good the assessor is. 
 3.  And a final artifact, on its own, is a strict information loss relative to the process that produced it.

The harness's contribution is exactly three matched fixes: 
ad1.  externalize state so continuity becomes a retrieval operation rather than a property of any one session; 
ad 2.  gate commits so acceptance becomes an independent check rather than a self-report; 
ad 3.  and retain typed trajectories so experience survives past the call that generated it, with rejected routes elevated to evidence only once reviewed. 

A simple runtime for real scientific experiments.

Prime Agent: Why AI Harnesses Matter More Than Models (IPython Kernel, ARC-AGI3, DeepSeek on DGX Spark)

In this video, I explain why AI harnesses are becoming more important than the models themselves, and I break down Prime Intellect’s new “Prime Agent” approach that replaces traditional JSON tool menus with a single IPython kernel. I cover how this recursive language model design keeps context “outside” the prompt in kernel memory, snapshots state to disk, and uses recursive sub-agents plus a self-improvement notebook that updates every 25 turns. I discuss the big ARC-AGI3 jump (including comparisons to OpenAI harness settings and Claude Opus 5), why the 95.5% result is self-reported, and concerns about benchmark cheating and reward hacking (including a Factorio admin console example). I also demo running DeepSeek V4 Flash locally on a DGX Spark cluster and share early internal harness comparisons on tokens, calls, and tool usage.

items.title: Ship Distributed Systems with Confidence
items.summary:
Fiodar Sazanavets is a Sr. Software Engineer specializing in large scale, data intensive distributed systems. He is a Microsoft MVP in Developer Technologies.

In this session, we’ll ask these questions:
- Why do distributed systems feel so hard to ship with confidence?
- What breaks when teams move from one app to many services?
- How does Aspire make cloud-native .NET development less overwhelming?
- How can developers manage databases, caches, queues, and containers without drowning in setup?
- Why is local orchestration such a big pain point for distributed apps?
- How does Aspire help teams see how all their services fit together?
- What are the most common mistakes teams make with service-to-service communication?
- How can developers test distributed systems before production exposes the problems?
- Why is observability essential for debugging cloud-native applications?
- How does the book help developers move from “it runs locally” to “it’s production-ready”?
- What should teams know before deploying Aspire apps to Azure Container Apps or Kubernetes?
- How can messaging and caching improve reliability in distributed systems?
- What security issues appear once an app becomes distributed?
- How can teams bring legacy .NET apps into a modern Aspire-based architecture?
- Who is this book for, and what will they be able to ship after reading it?

This is a live, interactive session, bring your questions for Fiodar.
 
We will also giveaway Ebooks to 2 lucky winners during the session. Comment #Ship to enter the raffle!
